clue.text: Pray the treatment may do you good

definitions.text: Pray the treatment may do you good

indicators.note: the letters of the first two words are given a working-over, a treatment that rearranges them

explanation.surface: A hopeful wish, said like a prayer, that some medical care will help.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: 'treatment' rearranges PRAY THE, and the full sentence describes the cure itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Psychological or physical remedial care is given in the hope that it will make the patient better.

clue.text: To follow without books can be hard work

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the following word surrounds the books

parts.note: to trail is to follow
AV is the Authorized Version of the Bible, the books

explanation.surface: Following along without books makes for a hard slog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' seems to mean lacking, but it means outside here.
explanation.definitionFit: Travail is painful toil, strenuous labour.

clue.text: Try to be a detective inspector

definitions.meaning: ... Morse is the detective inspector of Colin Dexter's novels and the TV series Inspector Morse

explanation.definitionFit: It means an attempt as noun or verb, and it is Inspector Morse's rarely used first name.

clue.text: In the middle of some dream on Gove's plans

indicators.note: some means only part of the words, the answer lies within them

explanation.surface: A fantasy runs through the policies of a politician named Gove.
explanation.walkthrough: Michael Gove was British Education Secretary when this appeared; 'plans' is surface padding.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean surrounded by or in the midst of, a preposition synonym.

clue.text: Measure of the Met's credit?

parts.note: the Met is London's Metropolitan Police, based at Scotland Yard, so the Met's is Yard's
tick is British slang for credit, buying on tick

explanation.surface: How much the London police can borrow.
explanation.walkthrough: Scotland Yard is the headquarters of London's police; 'on tick' is British for on credit.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard used for comparison or judgement is a measure.

clue.text: 2-star rating — and you can't get lower than that

definitions.text: you can't get lower than that

indicators.note: rating is read as assessing or reworking, so the letters of the two-word phrase are rearranged

parts.note: the figure 2 is written out as the word two

explanation.surface: A hotel or film earns two stars, which sounds about as bad as it gets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rating' rearranges TWO and STAR; the surface makes it a review score.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means in the poorest possible case, the lowest point an outcome could reach.

clue.text: A near disaster in the Colosseum?

indicators.note: disaster suggests something ruined, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Something almost went badly wrong in Rome's great amphitheatre.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the Colosseum as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: The Colosseum is the classic example of an amphitheatre for public contests.

clue.text: Dryad gets Allen round number at speed

indicators.note: round means the first name is wrapped about the abbreviation

parts.note: Woody Allen is the American film director
mph, miles per hour, measures speed

explanation.surface: A tree spirit gets a film director to circle a number at speed.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth a dryad is a female spirit of the trees.

clue.text: Correct ceremonial voice

indicators.note: voice tells us to say the word aloud and take its sound

parts.note: a rite is a ceremony

explanation.surface: A formal ritual tone of voice is the proper one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ceremonial' gives RITE, a noun from the adjective, as clues often do.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are adjectives meaning accurate or true.

clue.text: Old photographic process can do the work of a secretary

parts.note: a tin is a can

parts.words: do the work of a secretary
parts.note: secretaries type documents

explanation.surface: An old way of making pictures could handle office typing.
explanation.definitionFit: A Victorian method made photos directly onto thin iron plates; the name means that process.

clue.text: Vehicle has nothing to be heard

parts.note: an Audi is a German make of car
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A car arrives with nothing inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Audio refers to sound, material meant for listening rather than viewing.

clue.text: Sound source, or soundly peruse periodical

indicators.note: soundly tells us to take the word for peruse by how it is pronounced

parts.note: to peruse is to read
an organ is a newspaper or magazine published by an organisation

explanation.surface: Advice to read a magazine thoroughly, or a source of noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soundly' looks like 'thoroughly' but signals that READ is spoken, giving REED.
explanation.definitionFit: A harmonium-type instrument whose tones come from vibrating reeds is a source of musical noise.

clue.text: Incontinent — angel contrived to achieve painlessness

annotationWithheld.why: Incontinent — angel contrived to achieve painlessness (9) for ANALGESIA: 'Incontinent' (in continent) must give both ASIA and the container signal, one word doing two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: Incontinent — angel contrived to achieve painlessness

clue.text: Pedagogues' league sample heartless crackers

parts.note: the NUT is the National Union of Teachers, a British teachers' union

indicators.note: heartless means losing the middle, so the centre letter of the synonym goes

parts.note: to sample is to try

explanation.surface: A teachers' union sample turns out to be heartless crackers.
explanation.walkthrough: The NUT was Britain's National Union of Teachers. 'heartless' strips R from TRY to leave TY.
explanation.definitionFit: Crackers is British slang for mad, the same as being nuts or eccentric.

clue.text: Free to give quarter after battle

indicators.note: after places the compass letter following the battle name

parts.note: Loos was a First World War battle in northern France in 1915
a quarter is a compass point, here E for east

explanation.surface: After the fighting, an army is free to show mercy to the defeated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'give quarter' looks like showing mercy; here a quarter is a compass point, E.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unbound or unattached is at liberty, the adjective sense of not tied up.

clue.text: Do a gentle flip, when stretched

indicators.note: flip means turn over, so these letters are turned into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Doing a gentle somersault while limbering up.
explanation.definitionFit: Something drawn out to a greater length is lengthened or extended.

clue.text: In receipt of money sixties' youth cause trouble

indicators.note: being in receipt of something means taking it in, so one piece receives another

parts.note: income is money received
Mods were a 1960s British youth subculture of scooter-riding sharp dressers

explanation.surface: A young person of the sixties, given money, makes a nuisance of themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: Mods were a British youth movement of the 1960s.
explanation.definitionFit: To inconvenience someone is to put them out or bother them, a verb meaning to make difficulties.

clue.text: Shake-up for least pacy condition?

indicators.note: a shake-up reorganises things, so the following letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Reorganising the slowest runners because they are in a poor state.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the definition is broad; the answer is a trance-like state of rigidity.
explanation.definitionFit: Catalepsy is a medical state of rigid immobility, a condition in the medical sense.

clue.text: Having exhausted one's welcome, get injected but remain inside

annotationWithheld.why: Having exhausted one's welcome, get injected but remain inside (9) for OUTSTAYED: STAY (remain) inside OUTED, but no clue words give OUTED; 'get injected' fits no piece I can show
annotationWithheld.clue: Having exhausted one's welcome, get injected but remain inside

clue.text: Legal successor heard to gain from flying hazard

indicators.note: heard says the word for a legal successor is taken by its sound

parts.note: an heir is the person who inherits by law
to pocket is to gain or take for oneself

explanation.surface: An heir is overheard planning to profit from something dangerous in the sky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' is a link word joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A region of downdraught makes an aircraft drop suddenly, a danger to aviation.

clue.text: Being cornered made a lag run amok

indicators.note: running amok is moving wildly, so the letters go into disorder

explanation.surface: A convict, trapped, goes on a wild rampage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'run' is part of the letters, not the indicator; only 'amok' signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with corners or sharp angles is angular, the adjective sense.

clue.text: House tenancy rejected — or alternative …

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the word for tenancy is read backwards

parts.note: a let is a tenancy, a property rented out

explanation.surface: A tenancy on a house is turned down, so another option must be found.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis ties this to the next clue: a hotel is the alternative Russian lodging to a gulag.
explanation.definitionFit: Paired with the following clue, a hotel is another kind of Russian place to stay, an option instead of a labour camp.

clue.text: One space in penitential season is not too harsh

indicators.note: in places these pieces inside the season

parts.note: Lent is the Christian season of penitence before Easter
one is the Roman numeral I
an en is a printer's space

explanation.surface: One gap during Lent shows the fasting rules are not too strict.
explanation.definitionFit: Lenient means merciful or tolerant, so not too severe.

clue.text: … Russian place for censorship to contain smart student?

indicators.note: to contain means the censorship word holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: a gag is an order silencing speech, a form of censorship
U means upper-class, hence smart or posh
L stands for learner, a student

explanation.surface: A Russian institution of censorship holds a clever student.
explanation.walkthrough: U is a British label for upper-class usage. The ellipsis joins it to the previous clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gulag was the Soviet system of forced-labour camps, a notorious place in Russia.

clue.text: Fabled king in charge — it stands to reason

parts.note: King Log is the wooden king the frogs got in Aesop's fable

explanation.surface: A king from a fable is in command, which makes sense.
explanation.walkthrough: In Aesop, the frogs ask for a king and are given a log.
explanation.definitionFit: Reasoning is the subject of the answer, so something that stands to reason obeys it.

clue.text: Around Holland a number need character to make aware

indicators.note: around means the number goes round the country code

parts.note: eight is a number
NL is the international code for the Netherlands
an en is a printing measure, a character width

explanation.surface: Someone in the Netherlands needs a particular personality to inform people.
explanation.definitionFit: To inform or educate someone is to give them knowledge and understanding.

clue.text: Those last shall be first — that's moral significance

indicators.note: the final letter of the word is moved to the front, echoing the Bible phrase

explanation.surface: A biblical promise that the humble will rise, with its moral weight.
explanation.definitionFit: The ethos of a group is its guiding beliefs and moral character.

clue.text: Morning publication raised character

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means read upwards, so the pieces are reversed together

parts.note: AM is morning, ante meridiem
mag is short for magazine, a publication

explanation.surface: A morning newspaper boosted somebody's reputation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' reverses AMMAG as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: The third letter of the Greek alphabet is a character in the written sense.

clue.text: His plight could be a warning

indicators.note: could be suggests the letters might be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: Someone's predicament serves as a cautionary tale.
explanation.definitionFit: A moored vessel with a beacon warns ships away from dangerous waters.

clue.text: Naturalist puts end to middle, perhaps

indicators.note: the last letter of the name is moved into its centre

parts.note: Richard Mabey is a British naturalist and nature writer

explanation.surface: A nature expert relocates the tail end to the centre, possibly.
explanation.walkthrough: Richard Mabey is a well-known British writer on wildlife; moving his Y gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words express possibility without certainty, plain synonyms.

clue.text: Over a month a prophet turns and goes back

indicators.note: turns means the whole assembly is reversed
over means covering, so the prophet word wraps round the month

parts.note: a seer is a prophet
Dec is the abbreviation for December

explanation.surface: A prophet turns around and retreats after a month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over' puts the prophet round the month; 'turns' then reverses the whole assembly, so read the answer right to left to see the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To recede is to withdraw or move backwards, as tides do.

clue.text: Long ago, unknown date or 26

parts.note: in algebra y is an unknown quantity

indicators.note: the answer to 26 across is perhaps, which signals the letters might be rearranged

explanation.surface: A long time back, on some unknown date, or perhaps not.
explanation.walkthrough: The indicator is the answer to clue 26, read as 'perhaps', which rearranges DATE OR.
explanation.definitionFit: From the year dot is a British idiom for since the very beginning, a long time ago.
